channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: Experts urge caution as interest in industrial hemp grows
item.description: While industrial hemp offers a potential R660 billion opportunity for South Africa, experts warn that commercial success depends on more than just planting.

item.title: FMD vaccinations begin in Eastern Cape, industry flags supply concerns
item.description: The Eastern Cape Department of Agriculture rolled out foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) vaccinations in high-risk areas last week, but organised agriculture has warned that the current supply will not be enough to contain the disease if the outbreak continues.

item.title: Pork sector sees progress in disease response despite FMD and ASF challenges
item.description: South Africa’s pork industry is beginning to see tangible progress in the fight against foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) and African swine fever (ASF), with new regulatory amendments, vaccine roll-outs and additional abattoir approvals helping to stabilise the sector.

item.title: SA’s essential oils step into global spotlight
item.description: Karen Swanepoel, executive director of the Southern African Essential Oil Producers’ Association, spoke to Octavia Avesca Spandiel about South Africa’s essential oils industry and its rise from a small niche market to a quality-driven, globally recognised, and fast-growing business.

item.title: The updated Isuzu D-Max remains elusive in South Africa
item.description: Even though the face-lifted Isuzu D-Max was rolled out in other markets more than two years ago, South Africans are still waiting for the updated bakkie, writes The Citizen’s Charl Bosch.

item.title: FMD vaccines arrived, but delays raise questions about payment and coordination
item.description: In the middle of South Africa’s escalating foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) crisis, a consignment of 1,5 million urgently needed vaccine doses had already been in the country. However, the vaccines are not yet in the system meant to get them to farmers, exposing a gap between government assurances and the operational reality of the national vaccination roll-out.

item.description: South Africa is expected to exit the 2025/26 La Niña phase in April, moving towards neutral ocean and atmospheric conditions. Meteorologists say this shift may stabilise rainfall patterns, while agricultural economists

item.title: From planning to peak lay: building a profitable egg business
item.description: Mpumalanga poultry farmer Lebogang Mashego spoke to Octavia Avesca Spandiel, and shared practical insights on planning, building systems that work, breed choice, feed management, and markets to build a profitable and sustainable egg business.

item.title: Industry voices concern over Botswana’s fresh produce ban
item.description: Botswana’s repeated bans on South African fresh produce have raised concerns in the agriculture sector, with industry leaders saying the stop-start restrictions disrupt trade flows and make export planning difficult.

item.title: Bigger avocado harvest forecast amid challenging export season
item.description: The South African avocado industry entered its main harvesting season in March and is expecting a significantly larger crop, but stronger competition from Peru in key export markets is likely to temper optimism.
